market.name: AI Wearables (Global)
market.tagline: Devices you wear that listen, see and act through a personal AI.
market.definition: Body-worn devices whose main job is a personal AI: glasses, pendants, wristbands, clips and rings that capture what you say or see and turn it into answers, notes, reminders or actions.
market.allDescription: Compare capture, agency and availability across the full landscape.
market.author: Shamkhal Murtazaaliev
market.scope: Companies worldwide, judged on the same criteria. Most qualifying companies are US-based; this edition also covers Even Realities, Rokid, Xiaomi and Alibaba (China). Each profile gives the headquarters.
inclusion: Worn on the body: glasses, pendant, wristband, clip or ring
The AI is the point: an assistant or memory, not a health tracker, display or camera with AI added
For a person's own use, on sale or open for preorder
exclusions: Fitness and health trackers without a conversational AI
Display or XR glasses built mainly for screens and media
Devices announced but not yet open for orders

x.label: Always-on capture
x.rubric: 0 = listens or sees only while you press or hold it; 25 = wakes on a word, tap or gesture for short exchanges; 50 = records whole conversations or meetings when you switch it on; 75 = listens all day by default, with filtering or pausing; 100 = always-on audio and camera throughout the day

y.label: Agency
y.rubric: 0 = records or transcribes only; 25 = summarizes and answers questions about what it captured; 50 = proactive reminders, to-dos and insights pushed to you; 75 = takes actions in connected apps, such as sending messages or managing a calendar, with approval; 100 = runs errands and transactions on your behalf

yAlt.label: Availability
yAlt.rubric: 0 = announced with no way to order; 25 = open for preorder; 50 = shipping in limited quantities or one market; 75 = on sale broadly in at least one major market; 100 = in mainstream retail across many countries

companies.name: Persona
companies.description: Personal AI agent from Cal AI co-founder Zach Yadegari, in free beta over iMessage, with a $179 screenless wristband that summons it with a button or a flick of the wrist. The agent books flights, schedules, replies to email and makes purchases with approval.
companies.traction: Free iMessage beta with "a few thousand" users; wristband preorders reported in the five figures of revenue, shipping in December 2026. Also on the Personal AI Agents map.

capture.rationale: Activated by a button press or a flick of the wrist; it does not listen all the time.

agency.rationale: Runs errands such as flight bookings, scheduling and email, and makes purchases with approval.

availability.rationale: The band is on preorder for December 2026; the agent itself is in free beta.

lastRound.note: The $100M post-money valuation ($10M at $90M pre-money) was entered manually from a source that is not public. The $10M round led by Vine Ventures was reported by Dealroom on October 8, 2026; its stage was not disclosed.

companies.name: Nirva
companies.description: Eight-gram AI pendant, also worn as a bracelet, that passively listens all day but only to its wearer's voice, filtering out others, and turns it into a journal with mood and relationship patterns in a companion app.

founders.name: Wei Lyu
founders.role: Co-founder & CEO; former Meta Reality Labs product leader

founders.name: Hanying Hu
founders.role: Co-founder; founded a fashion and jewelry brand

companies.traction: Orders open in November 2026 at $249, with first shipments expected by year end; battery lasts up to three days.

capture.rationale: Always on, listening to the wearer's own speech and filtering out other voices.

agency.rationale: Journals the day and surfaces mood and relationship insights; it does not act in other apps.

lastRound.note: Follows an $8M seed earlier in 2026 from investors including Lightspeed and South Park Commons; sources differ on the new round's lead. Valuation not disclosed.

companies.name: Plaud
companies.description: AI note-takers: the card-sized Plaud Note and the wearable NotePin record meetings, calls and conversations when switched on, then transcribe, summarize and pull out to-dos in its app, sold with transcription subscriptions.
companies.traction: More than 3 million users (company); Bloomberg reported in June 2026 that it had passed $250M in annual recurring revenue and is targeting $500M in 2026 sales. Offices from San Francisco to Shenzhen and Tokyo.

capture.rationale: Records whole meetings and conversations when you switch it on.

agency.rationale: Transcribes, summarizes and extracts to-dos; answers questions about recordings.

availability.rationale: Sold online and in retail across the US, Japan, Europe and elsewhere.

lastRound.note: Largely bootstrapped: trackers list about $6M of outside funding, the latest a convertible note in April 2025, and reports of a mid-2025 valuation near $1B are unconfirmed.

news.title: Plaud reached $250 million in recurring revenue without a single venture dollar and is now targeting $500 million in 2026 sales

checks.title: Plaud site; no round or new figures since July 2026 found

companies.name: Sandbar
companies.description: Maker of Stream, a voice ring for note-taking rather than health tracking: touch it and whisper to capture thoughts, which its app organizes into notes, chats and dictation and can read back in your own voice.
companies.traction: First preorder batch sold out in 2025; a second batch was scheduled to ship in summer 2026 at $249 (silver) and $299 (gold), iOS first.

capture.rationale: Records only while you touch and talk to it.

agency.rationale: Organizes voice notes and answers about them; it does not act in other apps.

availability.rationale: Preorders with a summer 2026 shipping window; deliveries have not been independently confirmed.

lastRound.note: Reported to bring total funding to $36M after a $13M earlier round. Valuation not disclosed.

companies.name: Taya
companies.description: Maker of TAYA, an AI necklace for capturing passing thoughts: press its button and speak, and directional microphones pick up only the wearer’s voice, which the app turns into lists and cues to revisit.

founders.name: Elena Wagenmans
founders.role: Founder & CEO; Stanford-trained product designer and mechanical engineer, formerly building hardware at Apple

companies.traction: Initial preorder batch sold out before the seed round; preorders are open with an $89 refundable deposit, shipping is set for fall 2026, and the final price has not been announced.

capture.rationale: Records only between two presses of its button; the company says there is no passive mode.

agency.rationale: Its app organizes captured thoughts into lists and cues to revisit; it does not act in other apps.

availability.rationale: Open for preorder with a refundable deposit; shipping is planned for fall 2026 and has not been confirmed.

companies.name: Friend
companies.description: Always-listening AI companion worn as a pendant that hears your day and talks with you about it; the 2026 version ($249) speaks aloud, where the first texted its thoughts. It is built to keep you company rather than to take notes or do tasks.
companies.traction: On sale in the US; the original $129 pendant was retired for the talking version in 2026. The company paid $1.8M for the friend.com domain.

agency.rationale: Companion conversation by text; it does not organize information or take actions.

companies.name: Even Realities

agency.rationale: Answers, translation, teleprompting and navigation; limited actions in other apps.

companies.name: Rokid
companies.description: Hangzhou maker of Rokid Glasses, lightweight AI and AR glasses with a camera and display: an assistant answers what you see and hear, translates, records and prompts.
companies.traction: Sold in China and internationally after a Kickstarter that raised more than $4M; partnered with optician chain Krys in France in June 2026. Reported to be preparing a Hong Kong listing.

agency.rationale: Visual answers, translation, recording and teleprompting.

companies.name: Bee
companies.description: Always-listening wearable AI that turns your conversations into daily insights, reminders and to-dos; bought by Amazon, which launched the lighter, water-resistant Bee Frontier band-and-clip and the phone-mounted Bee Eclipse in October 2026.
companies.traction: Bee Pro ($11.99 a month) connects it to Alexa+, Amazon shopping, Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook and Apple Health, so Echo devices can answer questions about past conversations.

capture.rationale: Listens all day by default, with conversations processed into summaries.

agency.rationale: Proactive insights and to-dos, with connections to email, calendar and Alexa+ on the paid tier.

availability.rationale: On sale in the US through Amazon.

lastRound.note: Amazon acquired Bee in 2025; the price was not disclosed.

companies.name: Meta AI glasses
companies.description: Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta camera glasses and the Meta Ray-Ban Display with an in-lens screen and neural wristband. Meta AI answers about what you see, takes photos and video, sends messages and calls, and runs live sessions; Meta has said its Muse agent is coming to the glasses.
companies.parent: Meta Platforms — public (NASDAQ: META). The glasses are made with EssilorLuxottica; the parent's market capitalization is not a standalone product valuation.
companies.traction: Ray-Ban Display sold in the US at $799 and from September 2026 in the UK, Canada, Germany, France and Italy; a camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio ($349) shipped October 13, 2026.

capture.rationale: Wakes on "Hey Meta" with the camera on request; live sessions can watch continuously when started.

agency.rationale: Sends messages, makes calls and sets reminders through Meta's apps; the Muse agent is announced for the glasses but not yet live.

availability.rationale: In mainstream retail across many countries.

companies.name: Xiaomi AI Glasses
companies.description: Xiaomi’s camera glasses, sold in mainland China since June 2025. The Hyper XiaoAi assistant answers questions about what you see, translates speech and text, takes photos and video, and pays Alipay QR codes once you confirm the amount aloud.
companies.parent: Xiaomi Corporation — public (HKEX: 1810). The parent’s market capitalization is not a standalone product valuation.
companies.traction: Xiaomi says the glasses ranked third worldwide and first in mainland China by 2025 shipments, citing Omdia. Sold only in mainland China, from ¥1,999 at launch.

capture.rationale: Wakes on “Xiao Ai” or a touch; the camera records on request.

agency.rationale: Answers about what you see, translates, and pays Alipay QR codes after a spoken confirmation; no wider actions in other apps.

availability.rationale: On sale broadly in mainland China, online and in Xiaomi stores; not sold elsewhere.

companies.name: Alibaba Qwen Glasses
companies.description: Alibaba’s camera glasses, some with in-lens displays. They launched as Quark AI Glasses in November 2025 and were renamed Qwen Glasses in March 2026. The Qwen assistant answers about what you see, translates, takes meeting notes, gives proactive reminders, and is gaining voice-ordered food delivery, rides and hotel booking through Alibaba’s apps.
companies.parent: Alibaba Group — public (NYSE: BABA; HKEX: 9988). The parent’s market capitalization is not a standalone product valuation.
companies.traction: Sold in mainland China on Tmall, JD.com and Douyin and through more than 600 optical stores. The N1 and N1 Pro went on sale October 13, 2026 from RMB 2,899; Alibaba plans an international version within 2026.

capture.rationale: Wakes on “Hello Qwen” or a touch; the camera records on request. Proactive reminders draw on location, weather and calendar, not continuous capture.

agency.rationale: Voice-ordered food delivery, rides and hotel booking through Alibaba’s apps, rolled out in phases from late March 2026, and iris-verified payment on the N1 Pro; not yet independently tested.

availability.rationale: On sale broadly in mainland China, online and in optical stores; the international version is not yet on sale.
